question: The perimeter of a square is 248 m. Its area (in m² ) is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Side of the square = Perimeter ÷ 4 = 248 ÷ 4 = 62 m.

Area = Side² = 62 × 62 = 3844 m².

**∴ The correct answer is 3844 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Perimeter of the square = 248 m

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter = 4 × a (where a is the side length)

Area = a²

 
 a = 62 m
 a = 62 m
 P = 248 m
 Area = ?

**Calculations:**

⇒ 4 × a = 248

⇒ a = 248 ÷ 4

⇒ a = 62 m

⇒ Area = a²

⇒ Area = 62 × 62

⇒ Area = 3844 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 3844 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rectangle

Perimeter = 2 × (l + b) | Area = l × b | Diagonal = √(l² + b²)

Diagonal of a Square

Diagonal (d) = a√2 | Area can also be calculated directly as (d²) ÷ 2.

Rhombus

Perimeter = 4 × a | Area = (d₁ × d₂) ÷ 2, where d₁ and d₂ are the length of the diagonals.

Circle

Circumference = 2πr | Area = πr²
